A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ComFe research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across the restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original ComFe classification, robustness, OOD detection and ablation results, including extensive appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds training-time and GPU-memory comparisons in Table 4.

M1.justification: The stated contrastive loss changes from unnormalized prototype dot products in v3 Appendix A, Eq. (38), to L2-normalized prototypes in v4 Eq. (30). This is a limited revision of the documented objective; the core architecture and inference remain intact, and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The nine classification datasets, ImageNet generalization and robustness scenarios, and OOD datasets remain covered. The new efficiency comparison uses the existing CUB200 task; revised illustrative figures do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 removes the ResNet-50 linear baseline and frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 linear baseline from Table 1, although the latter remains in Table 2. The interpretable accuracy comparators and OOD comparator set are retained. New Table 4 compares training costs with ProtoPFormer and PIP-Net.

E3.justification: Table 4 introduces an efficiency evaluation on CUB200 using an 80GB A100 and batch size 64. It specifies ProtoPFormer ViT-L/16, PIP-Net ConvNeXt-tiny and ComFe DINOv2 ViT-L/14, with 200, 60 and 50 training epochs respectively. Existing classification, OOD and ablation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a computational-efficiency analysis in Table 4 and expands Figure 3's case explanations with background-prototype matches and similarity scores. Existing ablations, image-removal tests, register comparisons, reliability analysis and seed-sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both ablation appendices report five runs with mean and standard deviation. The seed information in Figures S9–S10 and the reliability analysis are retained; no new repeated-run practice, confidence interval or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports 34 seconds per epoch and 5GB for ComFe, versus 42 seconds and 28GB for ProtoPFormer, and 121 seconds and 42GB for PIP-Net under their stated configurations. Figures also add similarity scores, while Table 1 loses two baseline rows. Corresponding retained accuracy, robustness, OOD and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the mathematical definition of the contrastive loss to use normalized prototypes. v4 also makes the Bernoulli likelihood expression explicit. The hierarchical model, uniform-prior assumptions and Bayes derivations are retained; label renaming and relocated background-class equations do not constitute additional theoretical changes.

C1.justification: v4 newly claims ComFe is the first known interpretable approach scalable to ImageNet-1K and emphasizes modularity and training efficiency. Its abstract narrows the non-interpretable accuracy claim from obtaining better accuracy to competitive performance with comparable methods. The central prototype-based interpretability and robustness contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive discussion of pretraining differences and architectural compatibility when comparing with earlier interpretable methods. It also qualifies prototype utilization as applying to most bird species or commonly occurring. Existing discussions of background leakage, initialization sensitivity and OOD limitations remain, while the ProtoP comparison partly moves from the appendix into Discussion.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a concrete repository hyperlink where v3 only mentions GitHub, and Algorithm 1 explicitly updates the already-described learnable queries Q. Table 4 adds resource measurements. Conversely, v3's ImageNet training-time and memory estimates and its direct last-layer decoder-input explanation are removed.

R1.justification: v4 expands discussion of ProtoP-family methods and adds references including DINO, SPLICE, DeiT and directional statistics. It removes the general prototypical-learning overview and associated citations, including Prototypical Networks. Positioning emphasizes frozen-backbone modularity and ImageNet scalability while retaining the principal related methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. v4 reorganizes the likelihood and training-objective presentation, introduces a Discussion section containing some relocated material, and merges the former prototype-visualization appendix into Additional Results. The title, author information and terminology also change.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns, Figures 1–3 are substantially redesigned, and numerous segmentation overlays become confidence heatmaps. Figure 4 contracts from seven dataset columns to four. Table 4 is added, Table 1 is reorganized, and appendix displays are relocated and recaptioned.

improvement.justification: Table 4 adds direct evidence for training efficiency, revised figures make prototype explanations clearer, and the explicit repository link improves reproducibility information. These gains outweigh the limited loss of baseline context and earlier ImageNet resource estimates. The principal benchmark and ablation evidence remains unchanged, so the overall improvement is incremental.
